items.name: Location of Australia
items.formula: Entirely in the Southern and Eastern hemispheres; the Tropic of Capricorn crosses its middle.
items.example: Between the Indian and Pacific Oceans.

items.name: Size of Australia
items.formula: The smallest continent in area and population: 76.82 lakh sq km with Tasmania, about twice India.

items.name: Flattest and Desert Continent
items.formula: 94% of the land is below 600 m, so it is the "Flattest Continent".
items.example: Most of it is desert, so it is also the "Desert Continent".

items.name: Three physical divisions
items.formula: Eastern Highlands, Central Lowlands, Western Plateau.
items.example: Australia was part of ancient Gondwana land.

items.name: Great Dividing Range
items.formula: The Eastern Highlands, steep on the east; called the Australian Alps in New South Wales.
items.example: Mt. Kosciuszko (2230 m) is the highest peak.

items.name: Central Lowlands
items.formula: The Murray-Darling basin, the Lake Eyre basin and the Carpentaria Lowlands.
items.example: The world's largest artesian basin is here.

items.name: Western Plateau
items.formula: Covers 1/3 of Australia: the Great Sandy, Gibson and Great Victoria Deserts.
items.example: As old as the Deccan Plateau; MacDonnell and Musgrave ranges rise here.

items.name: River Murray
items.formula: Australia's main river (2590 km), from near Mt. Kosciuszko to Encounter Bay.

items.name: Lake Eyre and Uluru
items.formula: Lake Eyre is the largest lake and the lowest point; most lakes are salty.
items.example: Ayers Rock (Uluru), west of Lake Eyre, is the world's largest monolith.

items.name: Australia's seasons
items.formula: Opposite to the north: winter June to August, summer December to February.
items.example: A cold current makes the west hot and dry.

items.name: Rainfall in Australia
items.formula: Over 75 cm on the south-east, north and south-west coasts; below 25 cm in the interior desert.
items.example: Rain is unreliable in time and place.

items.name: Vegetation of Australia
items.formula: Few dense forests; temperate forests of eucalyptus (for oil and paper); acacia in the shrub lands.
items.example: Tropical forests on the north and north-east coast.

items.name: Australia's unique animals
items.formula: Platypus (egg-laying mammal), emu (largest flightless bird), kangaroo (national animal), koala, dingo.
items.example: About 60% of its native animals and birds are found nowhere else.

items.name: Farming in Australia
items.formula: Only 4% of land is farmed, on large modern farms; wheat is the main crop, about 70% of it exported.
items.example: The Murray-Darling basin is the main wheat area; sugarcane grows along the east coast.

items.name: Sheep and wool
items.formula: Australia is the leading producer and exporter of wool.
items.example: Nearly 75% of its sheep are Merino, which give fine wool.

items.name: Minerals of Australia
items.formula: World's largest bauxite deposits; iron ore exported to Japan; gold at Coolgardie and Kalgoorlie.
items.example: Uranium mainly in the Northern Territory (60%).

items.name: Population of Australia
items.formula: Very low density, about 3 per sq km; 85% live in towns.
items.example: New South Wales has 1/3 of the people; about 50% live in six capital cities.

mistakes.text: Australia is the smallest continent, yet about twice the size of India.
Australia's summer is December to February, when India has winter.
Australia's large flightless bird is the emu; South America's is the rhea.
